packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: fresh Claude subagents (Opus 5.5), image-only; packets 01 02 05 06 08 09 11 12 16 17 18 19 20 finished by a second reader after a crash, from the first reader's text and a coordinator hand-off naming tiles only
text:
packet-13 -- unverified image reading (blind; no identification seen in context)

LAYOUT SURVEY (from overviews image-001 and image-004)
- One parchment fragment, two faces. Reused as a wrapper/cover: corners cut diagonally, edges folded in (fold lines visible at left, right, top and bottom), sewing/tacket slits at left and right margins, a vertical crease/fold through the centre. Bottom edge torn/holed in the centre.
- Single column, about 21 lines visible per face (image-001: ~21 lines; image-004: ~21 lines). Gothic textualis bookhand, brown-black ink. No running titles visible; top margin present but cut. Lines at the bottom run onto the turned-in flap.
- image-001 face: heavily rubbed and stained, especially in the centre and right half (faded, smeared ink). A small red mark/paraph in the left margin at line ~8 ("re" ?), and some letters at line ~13 left ("fac"?) look reddish -- possibly touched in red; tentative.
- image-004 face: much better preserved, ink dark. A larger initial (red? looks brown-red) "N"? at line ~17 mid-line ("Nos ergo sorores et filie ...") marked with a vertical stroke before it -- probably a section opening; rubricated touch tentative. Superscript abbreviation marks frequent. A marginal mark at right of line ~10 ("a"?).
- No interlinear or marginal glosses seen on overviews. Text appears continuous prose (sermon/treatise-like), not text+commentary; tentative.
- Tiles: image-002 and image-003 are native tiles of the image-001 face (presumably upper/lower halves, overlapping); image-005 and image-006 are tiles of the image-004 face.

=== image-005 (tile, upper half of the image-004 face; lines 1-11 complete, line 12 cut at bottom edge) ===
Hand: gothic textualis; tironian et "7" = (et); superscript o after g = g(o) "ergo"; macrons for m/n. Punctuation: raised/medial point. A thin vertical stroke marks some sense breaks (l.6 after "est", after "ypoctas"; l.9 before "Similit'"). Red touch on the C of "Contra" l.7 (small red/orange stroke left of it).

Overlap: 006.01 = 005.09, 006.02 = 005.10 (not new text). New text from 006.03. Red: initial of "Similit'" 006.03 has a red touch; the initial "N" of "Nos" 006.07 is touched in red and preceded by a vertical stroke (section break). Bottom edge torn: central loss in lines 9-11.

=== image-002 (tile, upper half of the image-001 face; 10 lines + top of l.11) ===
Surface badly rubbed and water-stained; ink smeared/offset across the centre and right two-thirds. Only line-openings (left ~1/3) and scattered words are legible. I also made one blue-channel autocontrast crop: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-aaymeloglu--claude-assistant/beb42d25-081e-400b-8116-99c9c123a8f6/scratchpad/crops/p13-002-blue.jpg -- it helped little. Possible red touch on a letter at l.3 (after "dissoluit·") and at l.5 (before "anan?"). Left margin at l.8: small red-brown blot/paraph mark.

Verdict: no connected span of more than 2-3 words is secure on this tile. Not usable for a source match beyond isolated words.

=== image-003 (tile, lower half of the image-001 face) ===
Overlap: 003.01 = 002.09, 003.02 = 002.10 (not new text). New text from 003.03. Same rubbed surface; lines 3-7 have a few dark (better preserved / possibly retraced) words in the middle. The last two lines (003.10-11) are on the turned-in bottom flap, which was protected and is the clearest text on this face; torn in the centre. Red-brown touches at the start of 003.04 and 003.05 (initial letters), possibly rubrication.

Verdict: the face of image-001 yields only isolated words; the two flap lines (003.10-11) are the most checkable span on that face, but each is broken by the central tear.

LIMITATIONS AND SELECTION
- All four tiles opened (005, 006, 002, 003) plus both overviews; one extra contrast crop of 002. Not stopped on the image limit.
- Best-preserved and most useful for matching: the image-004 face (tiles 005/006), ~21 lines of connected prose, a discussion of oil (oil of mercy and charity, the Samaritan, oil of gladness, the oils of catechumens/chrism/the sick, David anointed), ending in an address beginning "Nos ergo sorores et filie ka-rissime". Gaps: l.1 centre (hole), ll.9-11 centre (tear).
- The image-001 face is largely illegible from rubbing/staining; only line-openings and the two flap lines are partly read.
- Which face is recto/verso not determined.
- Exposure: no proposed identification or prior reading was present in my context. I did nothing beyond the brief except the one contrast crop (allowed: "crops you make of them").
